issue_context.title: Unlit (unshaded) material property is ignored in glTF files
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0

### System information

windows 10

### Issue description

Gltf files that have KHR_materials_unlit (unshaded mode), won't be set to Unshaded in Godot.

### Steps to reproduce

The example project contains a gltf model that is suppose to be unlit/unshaded. However, Godot imports it incorrectly with its Shading mode set to per-pixel instead.

### Minimal reproduction project

[gltfUnshadedBug.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10877513/gltfUnshadedBug.zip)
comments:
There is no instance of `materials_unlit` anywhere in the codebase, so this glTF extension needs to be implemented.

Material parsing (for *importing* glTF scenes from Godot) is done here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/31eccb5501ddc92b4a17fd6ae33dca4ad217702c/modules/gltf/gltf_document.cpp#L3762-L3948

Material serialization (for *exporting* glTF scenes from Godot) is done here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/31eccb5501ddc92b4a17fd6ae33dca4ad217702c/modules/gltf/gltf_document.cpp#L3486-L3760

I suggest implementing both unshaded import and export in the same pull request. It should involve checking for the `KHR_materials_unlit` extension in the extensions dictionary, then calling `set_shading_mode(BasedMaterial3D::SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED);` on the material instance.

Can we get this working for line meshes as well? At the moment they always import as shaded.

Not sure how it works to do that, so maybe it not possible?
edit: I found that you can create a loader script that runs whenever loading a resource. So I am doing that to change the material whenever it is loaded and has lines in the mesh.

review_comments: I wonder if this could just be an empty variant instead as it is never checked. Dictionary initializes a few things that I don't think you would get with another variant

Some thing like this you mean ?
`extensions["KHR_materials_unlit"] = Variant();`

It didn't work. It yields a json file that looks like this : 
![2023-03-03_20-47](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3624853/222813033-71c6c95b-c2f1-450a-aa94-8c03b9dd68c7.png)

But the [spec](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/blob/main/extensions/2.0/Khronos/KHR_materials_unlit/README.md) defines it as an empty {object}, not a null : 

![2023-03-03_20-49](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3624853/222813242-b04d188c-5773-4966-ba46-c03347c17482.png)

And when importing the gltf file with the variant into blender, it fails, which is expected.

![2023-03-03_20-50](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3624853/222813472-4cd21409-c80c-4523-8f6d-63080b112d06.png)

Thanks for checking and for referring me to the spec. Indeed it looks like the spec requires an empty dictionary. In hindsight that makes sense as they may make additions to the extension in the future (unlikely for this particular extension, but still).
